Melchior Hoffman
mel'ki-or hof'man
n. (Melchior Hoffman, c. 1495–1543, apocalyptic Anabaptist preacher)
Hebrew Malki-or, king of light, through Latin Melchior; German Hoffmann, a farmer, a steward of a manor.

Definition · Webster 1828 · Scriptures · Corruption · Roots · Usage · Related

Biblical Definition

Melchior Hoffman was a Swabian furrier who became a lay preacher, moved from Lutheran to Anabaptist convictions, and carried an apocalyptic message through the Baltic ports and the Low Countries with great effect. He taught that the last days had come, that Strasbourg was the New Jerusalem, and that Christ would return in 1533; he presented himself at Strasbourg in that year expecting to be imprisoned briefly as the prophecy required, and remained in that prison for ten years until he died. He also taught that Christ's flesh was not taken from the virgin but brought from heaven through her, which denies the incarnation at the point where Scripture is most explicit. The dictionary records both the prediction and the Christology as errors, and names the rule that forbids the first: of that day and hour knoweth no man (Mat 24:36).

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) defines apocalyptic as containing or pertaining to revelation, and prediction as a foretelling, a prophecy.

expand to see more

APOCALYP'TIC, a. Containing or pertaining to revelation; disclosing; of or belonging to the Apocalypse.

PREDIC'TION, n. A foretelling; a previous declaration of a future event; prophecy.

FUR'RIER, n. A dealer in furs; one who dresses furs and makes them into garments.

INCARNA'TION, n. The act of clothing with flesh; the act of assuming flesh, or of taking a human body and the nature of man.

Key Scripture

Mat 24:36 — "But of that day and hour knoweth no man, no, not the angels of heaven, but my Father only."

Act 1:7 — "And he said unto them, It is not for you to know the times or the seasons, which the Father hath put in his own power."

Deu 18:20 — "But the prophet, which shall presume to speak a word in my name, which I have not commanded him to speak, or that shall speak in the name of other gods, even that prophet shall die."

Jer 23:21 — "I have not sent these prophets, yet they ran: I have not spoken to them, yet they prophesied."

Modern Corruption

He fixed a date for the return of Christ and spent his last ten years in a Strasbourg prison.

expand to see more

Two errors are named here. The first is date-setting, which Scripture forbids in terms that leave no room at all, and which every generation repeats because a date is more exciting than a watch. The second is the celestial-flesh Christology, held by Hoffman and after him by much of the Dutch radical wing: that the Son did not take his humanity out of Mary's substance but passed through her. That empties the incarnation of the very thing it was for, since what is not assumed is not redeemed, and a Saviour who did not take our nature cannot have borne our penalty in it.

The principle to recover is the plain prohibition and the discipline it imposes. “But of that day and hour knoweth no man, no, not the angels of heaven, but my Father only” (Mat 24:36). The risen Lord closed the question again on the mount of Olives: “It is not for you to know the times or the seasons, which the Father hath put in his own power” (Act 1:7). And the LORD's complaint against the uncommissioned prophet is exactly Hoffman's case: “I have not sent these prophets, yet they ran” (Jer 23:21).

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Greek hora (G5610), an hour, a definite time; Hebrew zuwd related to zid (H2102), to presume, to act proudly.

expand to see more

Greek hora (G5610) — an hour, a definite point of time; Matthew 24:36.

Greek kairos (G2540) — a season, a fixed and appointed time; Acts 1:7.

Hebrew zuwd (H2102) — to presume, to act proudly or presumptuously; Deuteronomy 18:20.

Hebrew ruwts (H7323) — to run, to hasten; Jeremiah 23:21.

Hebrew shalach (H7971) — to send, to commission; Jeremiah 23:21.

Usage

"“of that day and hour knoweth no man” (Mat 24:36) — Strasbourg, and the year 1533."

"“It is not for you to know the times or the seasons” (Act 1:7) — ten years in prison afterwards."

"“I have not sent these prophets, yet they ran” (Jer 23:21) — a furrier turned prophet."
